AMCA USA Certification — How It Works and Why It Matters

The complete guide for Kenyan students targeting international healthcare careers.

7 min read 20 May 2026 Certifications · Healthcare

AMCA USA Certification has become one of the most respected international healthcare credentials for caregivers, healthcare assistants, and nursing assistants. It is widely recognised across the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, and parts of Asia because it follows U.S. healthcare competency standards.

For GoCare learners, AMCA USA Certification is a powerful advantage — especially for those targeting overseas opportunities or seeking to strengthen their professional profile.

What Is AMCA USA?

AMCA (American Medical Certification Association) is a U.S.-based credentialing body that provides standardised healthcare certifications. These certifications validate your competence, professionalism, and readiness to work in clinical and caregiving environments.

Popular AMCA Certifications offered at GoCare:

  • Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA)
  • Patient Care Technician (PCT)

These certifications align with U.S. healthcare standards and are recognised globally.

Why AMCA USA Certification Matters

  1. Recognised Across the USA and Internationally — AMCA credentials are trusted by hospitals, clinics, long-term care facilities, and homecare agencies.
  2. Strengthens Overseas Job Applications — Employers in the USA, Canada, UK, and the Middle East prefer candidates with internationally benchmarked training.
  3. Enhances Your CV and Professional Identity — You stand out among applicants with only local qualifications.
  4. Supports Migration-Linked Healthcare Pathways — Especially for roles such as caregiver, HCA, CNA, and patient care technician.
  5. Complements Your Kenyan Qualification — You graduate with two certificates: a national TVET CDACC or NITA certificate and an international AMCA USA certificate. This combination increases your employability and salary potential.

Who Qualifies for AMCA USA Certification?

You qualify if you have any of the following:

  • Certificate in Healthcare Support Services – Level 5 (CNA)
  • Certificate in Caregiving – Level 4
  • Caregiver Course – Level II (NITA)
  • Home-Based Care Support – Level 3
  • Health Care Assistant (HCA)
  • Any recognised healthcare or caregiving qualification

GoCare students in eligible programmes automatically qualify for AMCA USA training and assessment.

Requirements for AMCA USA Certification

To register for AMCA USA Certification, you need:

  • A recognised healthcare or caregiving qualification
  • A valid national ID or passport
  • Basic English proficiency
  • Passport-size photo
  • Registration form (provided by GoCare)

How AMCA USA Certification Works

AMCA follows a structured process:

  1. Registration — You enrol through an approved training and examination centre such as GoCare.
  2. Training — You receive targeted preparation aligned with U.S. healthcare competencies.
  3. Assessment — You sit for the AMCA exam, which tests practical knowledge, clinical understanding, professional conduct, and patient care skills.
  4. Certification — Successful candidates receive an internationally recognised AMCA certificate.

What You Learn in AMCA USA Certification

AMCA focuses on practical, clinical, and patient-centred skills, including:

  • Vital signs monitoring
  • Infection control
  • Patient care procedures
  • Mobility and transfer techniques
  • Feeding and nutrition support
  • Bedside assistance
  • Communication and documentation
  • Safety and emergency response

Benefits of AMCA USA Certification

  1. Higher Employability — International certification increases your chances of being selected by employers.
  2. Better Salary Potential — Internationally certified caregivers and CNAs often earn more.
  3. Global Mobility — AMCA is recognised in the USA, Canada, UK, Germany, Ireland, UAE, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.
  4. Stronger Professional Identity — You gain credibility and confidence in your skills.
  5. Eligibility for Advanced Training Abroad — Some foreign institutions require international credentials for admission.

How Competency-Based Training Prepares You for the Real World

Why employers prefer GoCare graduates — and how competency-based education gives you practical skills that textbooks alone cannot deliver.

5 min read 01 May 2026 Career Tips

One of the most common frustrations among employers across Kenya is hiring graduates who have certificates but cannot perform the tasks those certificates claim to represent. Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET) was designed to solve exactly this problem — and it is the foundation of everything GoCare teaches.

What Is Competency-Based Training?

Competency-Based Education and Training (CBET) focuses on what a learner can do, not just what they have studied. Assessment is built around demonstrated skills — can you monitor a patient's vital signs correctly? Can you prepare a guest room to hotel standards? Can you manage an office filing system? If yes, you are competent. If not, you train until you are.

This is the model used by Kenya's TVET CDACC (Technical and Vocational Education and Training Curriculum Development, Assessment and Certification Council) — and it is the curriculum framework that all GoCare programmes follow.

Why CBET Produces Job-Ready Graduates

  • Skills are verified, not assumed — Every graduate is assessed on actual performance, not just written exams.
  • Training mirrors the workplace — GoCare's skills labs simulate real hospital wards, hotel reception desks, and kitchen environments.
  • Attachment is built in — All GoCare programmes include guaranteed industrial and hospital attachment, so students gain real work experience before graduation.
  • Employers trust TVET CDACC graduates — Because they know what competency assessment means.

How GoCare Implements CBET

  1. Skills labs — Modern, purpose-built labs where students practice clinical, culinary, and administrative tasks in simulated environments.
  2. Qualified assessors — GoCare's instructors are industry-experienced professionals, not just academics.
  3. Portfolio of evidence — Students build a documented record of competencies demonstrated over their training period.
  4. Hospital and industrial attachment — Real-world placement that bridges the classroom-to-workplace gap.
  5. International alignment — GoCare's programmes align with international standards, enabling graduates to earn additional certifications from SDC Canada and AMCA USA.

GoCare graduates don't just have a certificate. They have demonstrated competencies — and that is what employers are looking for.

What This Means for Your Career

When you graduate from GoCare, you are not starting from scratch in the workplace. You arrive with documented skills, clinical or practical experience, and in many cases an international certification alongside your national qualification. That combination sets you apart from the majority of applicants in any competitive job market.

Clear definitions, roles, qualifications, salaries, and career pathways — so you can choose the right course for your goals.

6 min read 04 Jun 2026 Healthcare

Many students confuse the terms Caregiver, Health Care Assistant (HCA), and Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) — yet these roles are very different in training level, responsibilities, salary, and international opportunities. This guide gives you a clear, simple, and accurate breakdown.

1. Who Is a Caregiver?

A Caregiver provides basic support to clients who need help with daily living activities, either at home or in a care facility.

  • Main duties: Bathing, grooming, feeding, mobility assistance, repositioning, companionship, light housekeeping
  • Where they work: Private homes, homecare agencies, elderly care centres, disability support homes
  • Entry: KCSE (Any Grade) or KCPE for Level 3
  • Courses: Certificate in Caregiving – Level 4, Caregiver Course – Level II (NITA), Home-Based Care Support – Level 3
  • Salary in Kenya: KES 20,000 – 45,000/month
  • Best for: Beginners entering the healthcare field

2. Who Is a Health Care Assistant (HCA)?

An HCA works in hospitals, clinics, and medical facilities under the supervision of nurses and clinicians, performing more clinical tasks than caregivers.

  • Main duties: Taking vital signs, Assisting nurses, Infection control, Patient hygiene, Feeding and mobility, Bedside care, Basic documentation
  • Where they work: Hospitals, Clinics, Nursing homes, Rehabilitation centres
  • Entry: KCPE or KCSE (Any Grade)
  • Courses: Certificate in Health Care Assistant (HCA), Caregiving – Level 4
  • Salary in Kenya: KES 25,000 – 50,000/month
  • Best for: Learners who want hospital-based experience

3. Who Is a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA)?

A CNA is the most advanced of the three roles — a licensed, clinically trained healthcare professional who works directly within medical teams in hospitals and care facilities.

  • Main duties: All HCA duties plus advanced patient monitoring, clinical procedures, emergency response, documentation and reporting to nurses
  • Where they work: Hospitals, Clinics, Long-term care facilities, International healthcare settings
  • Entry: KCSE D (Plain) and above
  • Courses: Healthcare Support Services – Level 5 (CNA)
  • Salary in Kenya: KES 30,000 – 60,000/month. International: KES 150,000 – 450,000/month
  • Best for: Learners targeting licensed, hospital-level, and international positions

A clear, accurate, and regulator-aligned guide to Kenya's training, assessment, and accreditation bodies — so you know exactly what your certificate means.

Kenya's education and skills-training ecosystem includes several regulatory bodies that oversee curriculum development, assessment, accreditation, and industry standards. Understanding the difference between TVET CDACC, TVETA, NITA, and KHPOA is essential when choosing a training institution or career pathway.

1. TVET CDACC — Curriculum Development, Assessment & Certification Council

Focus: Competency-Based Curriculum, Assessment & Certification (CBET). Established under the TVET Act 2013.

TVET CDACC is responsible for: developing competency-based curricula, registering industry assessors, conducting national assessments, issuing competency-based certificates, and ensuring training aligns with industry needs.

How to Apply for the UK Health & Care Worker Visa (Caregiver Pathway)

Your complete guide to working in the UK as a caregiver, HCA, or support worker from Kenya — steps, requirements, documents, and tips.

7 min read 08 Jun 2026 Healthcare

The United Kingdom continues to recruit caregivers, healthcare assistants (HCAs), and support workers from countries like Kenya due to a national shortage of healthcare staff. The UK Health & Care Worker Visa is the official pathway that allows qualified caregivers to work legally in the UK under licensed employers.

What Is the UK Health & Care Worker Visa?

This special visa category allows foreign healthcare workers to: work legally in the UK, work for licensed UK employers, bring dependents (spouse and children), access fast-tracked visa processing, pay reduced visa fees, and avoid the NHS surcharge.

Who Can Apply?

You qualify if you have:

  • A caregiving or healthcare qualification (Certificate in Caregiving Level 4, Healthcare Support Services Level 5 CNA, Caregiver Level II NITA, or HCA)
  • International certification (strongly recommended: SDC Canada or AMCA USA)
  • A job offer from a UK-licensed sponsor (the most critical requirement)
  • English proficiency (IELTS UKVI or equivalent)
  • Police clearance certificate
  • Medical exam (TB test)
  • Valid passport

Job Titles Eligible for the UK Care Worker Visa (SOC Code 6145)

  • Care Worker
  • Home Care Worker
  • Support Worker
  • Healthcare Assistant (HCA)
  • Nursing Assistant
  • Senior Care Worker
  • Domiciliary Care Worker

Step-by-Step Application Process

  1. Complete your qualification — Obtain your Caregiving Level 4, CNA Level 5, or equivalent GoCare certification
  2. Earn international certification — SDC Canada or AMCA USA (included FREE with eligible GoCare programmes)
  3. Search for a UK-licensed sponsor — Use the UK Home Office sponsor register to find approved employers
  4. Secure a job offer — Your sponsor issues a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS)
  5. Complete English proficiency test — IELTS UKVI or Duolingo English Test (DET) for UK
  6. Gather documents — Passport, academic certificates, international cert, police clearance, TB test results
  7. Submit your visa application online — Apply through the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) portal
  8. Attend biometrics appointment — At a UK Visa Application Centre (VAC) in Nairobi

Programme Overview

The Health Care Assistant / Caregiver programme at GoCare Training Institute is designed to equip learners with the practical skills and theoretical knowledge required to provide high-quality care to individuals in various healthcare settings.

Our curriculum focuses on patient safety, personal hygiene, basic nursing care, and effective communication. Graduates are highly sought after by hospitals and international agencies due to our hands-on training approach in modern labs.

What You'll Learn

01

Foundations of Caregiving

Understanding the role and ethics of a health care assistant.

02

Basic Nursing Procedures

Vital signs monitoring, wound care, and infection control.

03

Anatomy & Physiology

Basic understanding of human body systems and common disorders.

04

First Aid & CPR

Emergency response skills certified by international standards.

05

Nutrition & Dietetics

Planning and preparing healthy meals for patients with specific needs.

Academic Qualification

Open to KCSE graduates (Grade D and above) or equivalent.

Documentation

Copy of ID/Passport, KCSE Result Slip, and 2 passport photos.

Passion for Care

A genuine desire to help and care for others is highly valued.

Where are you located?

NAIROBI CITY CAMPUS: Nairobi CBD, GatKim Complex, 4th Floor, Temple Road.

THIKA ROAD / RUIRU CAMPUS: Thika Road Campus, Eastern Bypass, Kamakis, Ruiru.

National Accreditation & Regulatory Bodies

GoCare is fully registered, regulated, and licensed by Kenya's leading education and professional bodies. Our programmes meet the highest national standards · guaranteeing every qualification is valid, credible, and employer-recognised.

Ministry of Education · Republic of Kenya

GoCare operates as a fully registered TVET institution under the Ministry of Education, ensuring all programmes meet national legal and educational requirements.

TVETA · Technical & Vocational Education and Training Authority

TVETA licences and regulates GoCare as a recognized training institution. This confirms our facilities, trainers, programmes, and qualifications all meet national standards.

  • Facilities meet national standards
  • Qualified trainers
  • Approved programmes
  • Legitimate qualifications

TVET CDACC · Curriculum Development, Assessment & Certification

  • Industry-aligned curriculum

NITA · National Industrial Training Authority

GoCare is NITA-accredited to train and examine selected programmes, including Caregiver Level II. NITA certification is highly valued by employers in Kenya and internationally.

KHPOA · Kenya Health Professions Oversight Authority

KHPOA approves GoCare's medical and health sciences programmes (one year and above), enabling graduates to qualify for professional practising licences in hospitals and health facilities.

KNEC · Kenya National Examinations Council

GoCare is recognised by KNEC for selected programmes and examinations, providing national credibility and clear academic progression pathways for students.

General Requirements

All applicants must provide standard documentation regardless of the program level:

  • Identification: A valid National ID card or Passport.
  • Photographs: Two recent passport-sized photographs.
  • Academic Records: Certified copies of your KCSE/KSCE certificate or equivalent.

Program-Specific Criteria

Different academic levels have varying minimum grade requirements:

  • Diploma Programs: Minimum KCSE Mean Grade of C- (Minus) or a relevant Certificate qualification.
  • Certificate Programs: Minimum KCSE Mean Grade of D (Plain) or D+ (Plus) depending on the course.
  • Artisan / Short Courses: Open to KCSE graduates (any grade) or relevant prior experience.
